title: How Do Owls Turn Their Heads 270°? 🦉
description:
How can an owl turn its head 270 degrees without cutting off blood to its brain? Owls have tube-shaped eyes locked in their skulls, 14 neck bones instead of our 7, arteries that run through bony tunnels up to ten times wider than the vessel, and blood pools at the base of the head that keep the brain fed while it turns.

topic: How can an owl turn its head almost all the way around?
script: You'd black out, but owls spin their heads 270 degrees. How? First, an owl's eyes can't move. They're shaped like tubes, locked inside the skull. So to look around, the whole head has to turn. Second, extra bones. You have seven neck bones. An owl has fourteen, so the twist is shared out, a little at every joint. Third, the clever part: blood. Twisting would pinch the arteries, but an owl's run through bony tunnels, up to ten times wider than the vessel, so they don't get squeezed. And at the base of the head, the vessels balloon into little pools, storing extra blood for the brain, while the head is turned. So, if you had an owl's neck, what's the first thing you'd turn around to look at?
key_facts: Owls can rotate their heads up to about 270 degrees
Owl eyes are tube-shaped and fixed in the skull by a bony sclerotic ring, so they can't move their eyes
Owls have 14 neck vertebrae; humans have 7
The vertebral arteries pass through bony holes up to 10 times wider than the artery (Johns Hopkins, 2013)
Blood vessels at the base of the head balloon into reservoirs that keep the brain supplied while the head turns
